title: Anempathetic Sound / Playback Indifferent to the Event

source_refs.author: Michel Chion
source_refs.title: Audio-Vision
source_refs.cultural_context: Film-sound theory of music that continues without sharing the scene's feeling

observed_structure: A diegetic track is already playing and has a mood of its own.
The picture undergoes harm, shock, or loss.
The track does not bend, duck sympathetically, or stop for that event.
dramatic_operations: keep playback running with no sympathy for the event
let banal audio ignore the harm in the picture
make the indifference of the track the emotional fact
cinematic_affordances: a visible on-screen player so the track has a source
no score swell that agrees with the shock
the same tune or cartoon audible after the people are gone
level left low enough that the picture is still readable
cultural_scope: film-sound formal pattern; do not copy a signature song or a specific cartoon cue
misuse_risks: irony pasted on by a needle-drop with no on-screen source
a cheerful track that makes the harm unreadable
stopping the track at the scare so the indifference never lands

variables: whether the level changes at all
who is left able to hear it

transferable_structure: diegetic playback continues in an indifferent register and refuses to match the feeling of what the picture has just undergone
non_transferable_surface: a quoted song, a copied cartoon soundtrack, or a famous ironic needle-drop
